summary: Test whether per-level Hall conditions with short completions glue one matching with constant loss.
Test position-aware cell exits and an Orlicz truncation of edge loads for one-scale (4,4) counts, then price scale coupling.
Prove or refute simultaneous matching tail counts at two unequal levels for every pair on the curve.
Use one optimal-transport potential to couple tail levels; overcome its excess conjugate penalty and uncontrolled off-sample gradient.
Read Aizenman–Wehr and test whether random-field response tails explain correlations between matching scales.
Check whether tree-based oblivious routing has constant competitive ratio for grid Orlicz costs, or a relevant lower bound.
Find a Gaussian-large convex body adapted to psi_4 flow cost and express the divergence constraint as a signing problem.
Hash drafts sent to reviewers and reject unreviewed additions or changes at finalization.
Require error terms to be compared explicitly with the scale of each bound-based decision.
Check that applications of newly declared claims account for every registered hypothesis on the actual instance.
Check Owed attempt placement before append and honor same-turn build closures in queue validation.
Require evidence for both directions when summaries claim equivalence, exactness, or an only-missing condition.
Derive the general-pair matching-to-discrepancy reduction and compare its function class with T4's grid discrepancy problem.
Prove or refute a constant-loss converse: does a low-cost matching force small penalized discrepancy?
Test the Hopf–Lax converse specifically on scaled Leighton–Shor functions to exclude all pairs below the curve.
Bound interpolated tube density of optimal exponential-cost matchings by O(N), which would establish the flow converse.
Transfer finite convex grid-flow duality to continuous discrepancy without losing the pairing or bounded-flow cost.
Show each deferred Owed attempt beside the latest promised attempt and require the reviewer brief to include that comparison.
Check reviewer credits in Verification gates against the actual saved report, including unverified sketches.
Reject Passed leads whose break point compares hypotheses but never states what the proposed translation yields.
List post-review sentence changes and their numeric conditions for rechecking before append.
Require structural or dual record searches beyond a draft's own wording, distinguishing author searches from reviewer searches.
Flag unchanged summaries when the claim or item they summarize changed after review.
Extend Bernstein chaining from sufficiently wide tent bands to thin bands, plateaus and general single-level class functions.
Determine whether the pyramid threshold is sharp for uniform Lebesgue discrepancy bounds below logarithmic levels at (4,4).
Replace the discrete-flow event by upper-tail cell-count bounds on grids with kappa below four.
Test a general variance/kernel obstruction to linear flows above exponent two, starting with heat-smoothed Poisson flow.
Match every uniformly quantified parameter in a probabilistic proof to the union-bound step covering it.
Construct anisotropic matchings refined across levels from the outset, avoiding post-hoc gluing of independent matchings.
Block commits that stage a file after an uncorrected failed edit, using live hook markers rather than delayed transcripts.
Resolve missing-condition commit warnings before base synchronization, after calibrating false refusals.
Try rerouting good matchings to O(N) tube density at constant cost, or identify the concentration obstruction.
Compare exact assignment-dual potentials with the gradient-penalized class, or refute a curve pair directly through those potentials.
Extend fine-grid, cut-cell and guided-chain bounds from (4,4) to other interior pairs using rectangular cells.
List all alternative forms of a cited bound, including min terms and cases, before selecting one for an application.
